solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Assist beside outside broadcast spot

indicators.note: beside means next to, so the two chunks stand side by side, with the broadcast letters written first

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for a programme made away from the studio
to assist or wait on someone

explanation.surface: A TV runner helping out next to the outside broadcast van, looking for a good spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'spot' as a place for the broadcast van; it is the verb, to notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to spot something is to catch sight of it, and to observe is to notice.

clue.text: Greyish-white feline caught this female bird

parts.note: oyster is the name of a pale greyish-white colour
a female pointed at as 'this' one

explanation.surface: A pale grey cat has caught a hen bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Oyster as a colour name is the unfamiliar step; the surface makes the cat the bird's hunter, when the cat is inside its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the oystercatcher is a black-and-white wading bird of the shoreline.

clue.text: Problem about rising pastry layer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the problem wraps around the pastry
in a down clue a word that rises is read from the bottom up, so it comes out backwards

parts.note: a pastry case with a filling

explanation.surface: A baker's problem with pastry that will not rise properly into layers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' looks like baking talk about pastry; in a down clue it is what turns the tart upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a stratum is a layer, of rock in geology or of people in society.

clue.text: Called the last in assembly spare

indicators.note: the last in a group is its final member, so only the final letter of assembly is used

explanation.surface: Someone called the latecomer to a school assembly surplus to requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' is the adjective meaning lean and thin, not the one meaning extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A less common sense: a spare figure is lean and long-limbed, which is what rangy describes.

clue.text: Record that is introduced to make legal claim over bouquets

indicators.note: introduced to means brought into, so the record and 'that is' go inside the legal claim
in a down clue, turning a word over flips it so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: to bring a case in court
a written record, like a ship's

explanation.surface: A court record showing someone sued over a delivery of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquets' are compliments here, not flowers; the legal surface keeps you among lawyers and florists.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: bouquets are words of praise, and eulogies are speeches of praise.

clue.text: Scattered boxes with energy

parts.note: boxes as a boxer does in practice

explanation.surface: Cardboard boxes strewn about by an energetic mover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' looks like a noun for cartons; it is the verb, fights in practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: things thinly spread out over an area are both scattered and sparse.

clue.text: The brothers overturned, missing hard ice

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so in a down clue the letters read from the bottom up
missing means lacking, so the letter for hard is left out

parts.note: H = hard, as on pencils; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: Two brothers upended and slipping because the hard ice they expected was missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard ice' reads as one phrase; hard is the letter to drop and ice is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialised sense: an ice is a frozen dessert, and a sorbet is a water ice made without cream.

clue.text: Fuss over helping worship

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the fuss is written first

parts.note: fuss and bother, as in much ado
a helping, a fixed portion of food

explanation.surface: Complaining about how much food you get, when you should be praying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' looks like a verb about worship; it is a noun, a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: worship and adoration are both deep reverence, especially towards a god.

clue.text: Tongue was hurt on hot pepper, not cold

indicators.note: something hurt is damaged and bent out of shape, so the letters of 'was' are put out of order
not cold means the letter for cold is taken out
in a down clue, on means placed on top, so the rearranged letters come first

parts.note: a hot pepper, in its one-L spelling
C = cold, as on taps; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: Someone whose tongue was burnt by a chilli pepper.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'tongue' the thing in your mouth burnt by the pepper; it is a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue in its sense of language: Swahili is the lingua franca of East Africa.

clue.text: Foreigner carrying large variety of fig?

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside, so the foreigner has the letter for large within it

parts.note: L = large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: An immigrant carrying a big load of figs.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: the strangler fig is one variety of fig.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the strangler fig is a tropical fig that grows around a host tree and smothers it.

clue.text: Town centre in Rome with a good hospital

indicators.note: the centre in a word is its middle, so only the two central letters of Rome are used

parts.note: H = hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A town centre in Rome that has a decent hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Town centre' reads as one phrase; the definition is Town alone, and centre goes with Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Omagh is the county town of County Tyrone in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Dealing with those that live on earth I call "our truth", in a way

definitions.text: Dealing with those that live on earth

indicators.note: put in a different way, so the letters of the quoted words are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A preacher proclaiming a creed for all the earth's inhabitants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those that live on earth' sounds like people; it means plants, which live in soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic paraphrase: horticultural means concerned with growing plants, which are rooted in the earth.

clue.text: Record attempt by bridge players

parts.note: East and North, two of the four seats at bridge

explanation.surface: A pair of bridge players having a go at a record.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named North, South, East and West, so any two of N, S, E, W can be 'bridge players'.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: an entry is an item recorded in a log, diary or ledger.

clue.text: Run after I angered drunken soldier

indicators.note: after means following, so the letter for run is placed at the end
a drunken walk lurches all over, so the letters of 'I angered' are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone running off after upsetting a drunk soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken soldier' reads as one phrase; drunken belongs to the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a grenadier is a soldier, originally one who threw grenades, now of a Guards regiment.

clue.text: Perhaps German person arriving outside chambers

indicators.note: outside means on the outer side, so the person arriving is wrapped around the chambers

parts.note: one who comes, as in 'all comers'
chamber pots, in the old slang plural

explanation.surface: A German visitor turning up at a barrister's chambers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps German' reads as a nationality; it names the English composer Edward German. 'Chambers' means chamber pots, not rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Edward German was an English composer of light opera, so a German can be a composer.

clue.text: Best open hotel chain

parts.note: H = hotel in the phonetic alphabet
a line of things one after another

explanation.surface: An advert for the finest newly opened hotel chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' is the verb, to defeat, not the adjective the advert suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to best an opponent is to defeat them, and to overthrow is to bring down by force.

clue.text: Right car to go around one Italian city

indicators.note: to go around something is to encircle it, so the letters for right and car close around the one

explanation.surface: Finding the right car to tour an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The one sits between R and the car, so the pair together goes around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Rimini is a resort city on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Get scared of sound in swamp

indicators.note: in means inside, so the word for sound sits within the swamp

parts.note: a low marshy area, as in the Fens of eastern England
sound as in of sound mind: healthy, correct

explanation.surface: Someone scared of noises out in the swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' means noise in the surface; here it is sound as in healthy. 'Get scared' is causative, to make someone scared.
explanation.definitionFit: A causative sense: to get someone scared is to make them afraid, to frighten them.

clue.text: Identified gadget to be thrown out

indicators.note: thrown out of place, as a machine is thrown out of alignment, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A gadget, once identified as useless, gets binned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown out' reads as discarded; it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: something tagged has been labelled, marked out and so identified.

clue.text: Relative with really good degree

explanation.surface: A family member with a first-class degree.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'really good degree' as one idea; really good stands alone and degree is a separate chunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a grandmother is a relative, and grandma is the familiar form.

clue.text: Company reportedly pursuing £1000 wine

indicators.note: a report is heard, so the word for company is taken by its sound, not its spelling
pursuing means chasing behind, so the company comes after the thousand

parts.note: a company, as of sailors, said the same as the French word for a growth

explanation.surface: A firm, in the news, splashing a thousand pounds on a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a firm chasing money; 'company' is a crew. Grand cru is French for a top-ranked vineyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a grand cru is a wine from a vineyard of the highest official classification.

clue.text: One who does raise spirits around party regularly

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for raise spirits wraps the party letters
at regular intervals, so every other letter of party is taken

parts.note: second and fourth letters of pArTy

explanation.surface: A person who livens up a party now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' is slang for swindles, as in 'I've been done', not the ordinary 'does'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang sense: to do someone is to swindle them, so one who does is a cheater.

clue.text: One hard-working old judge in strange rant

indicators.note: in means inside, so old and judge sit within the other letters
strange means odd or unfamiliar, so the letters of rant take an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: A diligent retired judge caught up in an odd tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom 'to work like a Trojan', meaning to work very hard.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: from 'work like a Trojan', a Trojan is someone who works tirelessly.

clue.text: Where one's warm and rather abandoned in embrace

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and uninhibited, so the letters of rather run wild into a new order
in means inside, so those letters go within the embrace

explanation.surface: Someone warm and uninhibited in a lover's arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' suggests passion; it is the signal to rearrange. A hearthrug is the rug in front of a fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic paraphrase: a hearthrug lies before the fire, the place one sits to get warm.

clue.text: Lively right after beer

indicators.note: after means following, so the letters for right are written behind the beer

explanation.surface: Perking up straight after a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends a beer makes you livelier; right is just the abbreviation RT.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: lively and alert both describe someone quick and wide awake.

clue.text: Expert answer with a lot of complexity

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the word for complexity loses its last letter

parts.note: DEPTH, complexity, without its final H

explanation.surface: A specialist's answer that is very complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of complexity' reads as 'very complex'; it asks for most of a word meaning complexity.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: an adept is someone highly skilled, an expert.

clue.text: Legal clause added by one in the saddle?

definitions.meaning: an extra clause tacked onto a bill or contract
a person sitting on a horse or bicycle

explanation.surface: A jockey writing an extra clause into a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'by' reads as authorship, as if the jockey added the clause; it only joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an extra clause appended to a legal document, and a person on horseback.

clue.text: One who'll go far as a jewellery worker?

definitions.text: One who'll go far as a jewellery worker?

parts.note: reads as someone with a bright career ahead; literally, someone who travels great distances
a craftsman who mounts stones, here the black gemstone jet

explanation.surface: A craftsman at the jeweller's bench destined for great things.
explanation.walkthrough: A jet setter would be someone who sets jet, a black stone used in jewellery; a jet-setter is a rich person always flying abroad, who literally goes far.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: the jet-set travel the world by plane, and the question mark admits the jewellery reading is a pun.

clue.text: Wine after cheddar? This port's essential for that

indicators.note: after means following, so cheddar is written first and wine behind it
the essential part is the core, so only the inner stretch of 'cheddar wine' is kept, the tail of one word and the head of the next

parts.note: first letters of the word wine, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: Pairing a wine with a cheese board, and naming a port that suits it.
explanation.walkthrough: You must first put the words in the order the clue asks, cheddar then wine, before the port appears across the join. Darwin is the port city of Australia's Northern Territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Darwin is the main port and capital of Australia's Northern Territory.

clue.text: With nothing odd — in fact, surreally so?

definitions.text: With nothing odd — in fact, surreally so?

indicators.note: keeping nothing from the odd-numbered positions leaves only the even letters

parts.note: even letters of iN fAcT sUrReAlLy

explanation.surface: A deadpan claim that nothing strange is going on, when it is surreal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: something with nothing odd about it is natural, and the question mark admits that surreal is hardly natural.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: read straight, 'with nothing odd' describes what is normal and unforced, which is natural.
